record.paper_title: Two open problems in graph theory
record.original_question: Let G and H be finite simple graphs with at least three vertices. If the multiset of vertex-deleted subgraphs of G is identical to the multiset of vertex-deleted subgraphs of H, must G and H be isomorphic?

evidence.quote: Reconstruction Conjecture. Let G and H be graphs on a finite vertex set with at least three vertices. Then if [Gv : v 6 VG] and [Hw : w € VH] are the same, so are G and H .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G and H be finite simple graphs, each having at least three vertices. For a graph X with vertex set V(X), define the deck of X to be the multiset D(X) = {{X - v : v ∈ V(X)}}, where X - v denotes the subgraph obtained from X by deleting the vertex v together with all edges incident to v, and where vertex-deleted subgraphs are considered up to isomorphism.

Prove or disprove: if D(G) = D(H) as multisets of isomorphism classes of graphs, then G and H are isomorphic.
artifact.status_search_result: This is the Reconstruction Conjecture of Kelly and Ulam (1941/1942), which remains a famous open problem in graph theory. It has been verified for many graph classes (e.g., trees, regular graphs, disconnected graphs, maximal planar graphs) and for all graphs up to 11 vertices, but no proof or counterexample is known in general.

status_evidence.title: Reconstruction conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Informally, the reconstruction conjecture in graph theory says that graphs are determined uniquely by their subgraphs. It is due to Kelly and Ulam... The conjecture remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The Reconstruction Conjecture is still open in general, though verified in many special cases.
